- Overestimate prices in the short term (1-3 days) after sentiment spikes (sentiment > 0.5), especially when forecast peaks are followed by sharp declines.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (sentiment < 0.3) and recent price action shows mean reversion or consolidation.
- Avoid overreacting to recent price spikes — model tends to overshoot after a 3-5 day uptick, then corrects downward.
- When sentiment is rising steadily (e.g., 0.6–0.8 over 3+ days), model often overweights the momentum and fails to account for regulatory or policy-induced mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates the final 5–7 days, especially if sentiment is high — adjust downward by 1–2% for the last 7 days if sentiment > 0.6.
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings > 0.2 per day), model tends to lag the true price by 1–3 days — use a 1-day lag correction for volatile sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is high but price is consolidating (e.g., 0.7–0.8 with low volatility), model often overestimates the peak — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 7-day high.
